english: I opened an account at the bank.
grammar: 계좌 (gyejwa) = bank account; 계좌를 만들다 = to open an account.

english: I opened a new bank account.
grammar: 통장 (tongjang) = bankbook/account; 개설하다 = to open (an account).

english: I want to open one more account.
grammar: Counters use native numbers: 하나 (hana) = one; 하나 더 = one more.

english: There's hardly any balance in my account.
grammar: 잔액 (janaek) = balance; 얼마 없다 = there's barely any left.

english: I made a separate salary account.
grammar: 따로 (ttaro) = separately; 월급 통장 = a dedicated salary account.

english: I updated my bankbook after a long time.
grammar: 통장 정리 (tongjang jeongni) = printing/updating the bankbook.

english: I waited at the bank counter.
grammar: 창구 (changgu) = teller window/counter; 에서 marks where you wait.

english: I take a number and wait.
grammar: 번호표 (beonhopyo) = queue ticket; 뽑다 → 뽑고 = take one and...

english: I forgot my account PIN.
grammar: 비밀번호 (bimilbeonho) = password/PIN; 잊어버리다 = to forget.

english: You have to bring your ID.
grammar: -아/어야 해요 = have to: 가져가야 해요 (gajyeogaya haeyo) = must take it.

english: I signed up for internet banking.
grammar: 신청하다 (sincheonghada) = to apply for/sign up for.

english: I check my balance on the app.
grammar: -(으)로 = by means of: 앱으로 (aebeuro) = via the app.

english: I put money into my account.
grammar: 넣다 → 넣었어요 (neoeosseoyo) = put in; 통장에 = into the account.

english: I withdrew a little cash.
grammar: 찾다 = to withdraw money: 돈을 찾아요 = take money out.

english: The bank closes at four.
grammar: Clock hours use native numbers: 네 시 (ne si) = four o'clock.

english: I pay into a savings plan every month.
grammar: 적금 (jeokgeum) = installment savings; 매달 = every month.

english: I signed up for a three-year savings plan.
grammar: -짜리 = one worth/of: 삼 년짜리 (sam nyeonjjari) = a three-year one.

english: I save 500,000 won each month.
grammar: Money uses Sino numbers: 오십만 원 (osimman won); -씩 = each/apiece.

english: I want to build up a lump sum.
grammar: 목돈 (mokdon) = a lump sum, a big chunk of money.

english: The deposit interest is too low.
grammar: 예금 (yegeum) = deposit; 이자 = interest; 낮다 → 낮아요 = is low.

english: The interest rate is 2 percent.
grammar: 퍼센트 (peosenteu) uses Sino numbers: 이 퍼센트 = two percent.

english: A saving habit is important.
grammar: 저축하다 (jeochukhada) = to save money; 습관 = habit.

english: I'm saving an emergency fund separately.
grammar: 비상금 (bisanggeum) = emergency money; 모으다 → 모으고 있어요.

english: I save money little by little.
grammar: 조금씩 (jogeumssik) = little by little, bit by bit.

english: My savings plan matures next month.
grammar: 만기 (mangi) = maturity date of a deposit/savings plan.

english: When it matures, I'll have a lump sum.
grammar: -(으)면 = when: 되면 (doemyeon) = when it becomes/matures.

english: I'll travel with that money.
grammar: -(으)로 = with/using: 그 돈으로 (geu doneuro) = with that money.

english: I save diligently.
Looking at my bankbook, I feel proud.
grammar: 뿌듯하다 (ppudeuthada) = to feel proud/fulfilled (first person).

english: I set a target amount.
grammar: 금액 (geumaek) = amount of money; 목표 금액 = target amount.

english: I got a new credit card.
grammar: 신용카드 (sinyongkadeu) = credit card.

english: I only use a debit card.
grammar: 체크카드 (chekeukadeu) = debit card; -만 = only.

english: My card bill came out high this month.
grammar: 카드값 (kadeukap) = card bill; 나오다 → 나왔어요 = came out.

english: I paid in installments.
grammar: 할부 (halbu) = installment payment (vs 일시불 = lump sum).

english: I bought it in three monthly installments.
grammar: 개월 uses Sino numbers: 삼 개월 (sam gaewol) = three months.

english: I paid all at once.
grammar: 결제하다 (gyeoljehada) = to make a payment; 일시불 = lump-sum.

english: I swiped my card way too much.
grammar: 긁다 → 긁었어요 (geulgeosseoyo) = swiped (a card), slang for overspending.

english: Next month I'll cut back on the card.
grammar: 줄이다 → 줄일 거예요 (juril geoyeyo) = will reduce it.

english: I've racked up a lot of card points.
grammar: 쌓이다 → 쌓였어요 (ssayeosseoyo) = piled up, accumulated.

english: I lost my card, so I reported it right away.
grammar: 신고하다 (singohada) = to report (a loss/incident) to authorities.

english: My card limit is maxed out.
grammar: 한도 (hando) = limit; 차다 → 찼어요 = got full/reached.

english: I find cards more convenient than cash.
grammar: -보다 = than: 현금보다 (hyeongeumboda) = than cash.

english: I checked my card statement.
grammar: 명세서 (myeongseseo) = an itemized statement/bill.

english: I transferred money to a friend.
grammar: 이체하다 (ichehada) = to transfer money between accounts.

english: I sent it straight to the account.
grammar: 송금하다 (songgeumhada) = to send/remit money.

english: A transfer fee was added.
grammar: 수수료 (susuryo) = fee/commission; 붙다 → 붙었어요 = got attached.

english: I pay the rent by bank transfer.
grammar: 월세 (wolse) = monthly rent; 계좌로 = to/via the account.

english: It goes out by auto-transfer every month.
grammar: 자동이체 (jadong-iche) = automatic transfer/direct debit.

english: I sent money to the wrong account.
grammar: 잘못된 (jalmotdoen) = wrong/mistaken (before a noun).

english: I called the bank and cancelled it.
grammar: -아/어서 = and then: 전화해서 (jeonhwahaeseo) = called, and then...

english: I deposited money into the account.
grammar: 입금하다 (ipgeumhada) = to deposit money in (opposite of 출금).

english: I withdrew money from the ATM.
grammar: 현금인출기 (hyeongeuminchulgi) = ATM/cash machine.

english: There's a set withdrawal limit.
grammar: 출금 (chulgeum) = withdrawal; -아/어 있어요 = is (in a state).

english: A lot of money went out this month.
grammar: 나가다 → 나갔어요 (nagasseoyo) = went out/was spent.

english: I put loose change in the piggy bank.
grammar: 잔돈 (jandon) = loose change; 저금통 = piggy/coin bank.

english: I exchanged currency at the bank.
grammar: 환전 (hwanjeon) = currency exchange; 환전을 하다 = to exchange money.

english: I changed it to dollars before the trip.
grammar: 바꾸다 → 바꿨어요; 달러로 = into dollars.

english: I took out a loan at the bank.
grammar: 대출 (daechul) = loan; 대출을 받다 = to take out a loan.

english: I'm still paying off my student loan.
grammar: 갚다 → 갚고 있어요 (gapgo isseoyo) = am paying back.

english: The loan interest is such a burden.
grammar: 부담스럽다 → 부담스러워요 (budamseureowoyo) = feels burdensome (ㅂ-irr).

english: I have to pay interest every month.
grammar: 이자를 내다 (ijareul naeda) = to pay interest; -아/어야 해요 = have to.

english: I want to pay off the loan fast.
grammar: 대출금 (daechulgeum) = the loan principal/amount owed.

english: I paid off a bit of the principal this month.
grammar: 원금 (wongeum) = principal (vs 이자 = interest).

english: Interest rates went up again.
grammar: 금리 (geumni) = interest rate; 오르다 → 올랐어요 = rose.

english: I borrowed money from a friend.
grammar: 빌리다 → 빌렸어요 (billyeosseoyo) = borrowed.

english: I'll definitely pay it back next month.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 = I promise to: 갚을게요 (gapeulgeyo) = I'll pay it back.

english: I have no debt, so I feel at ease.
grammar: 빚 (bit) = debt; 빚이 없다 = to be debt-free.

english: If you take a loan, interest builds up.
grammar: -(으)면 = if: 받으면 (badeumyeon) = if you take/receive it.

english: I manage my credit score well.
grammar: 신용 점수 (sinyong jeomsu) = credit score; 관리하다 = to manage.

english: I'm looking for a bank with low interest.
grammar: 낮은 (najeun) = low (before a noun): 이자가 낮은 은행.

english: I got a loan consultation.
grammar: 상담 (sangdam) = consultation; 상담을 받다 = to get advice.

english: I pay taxes every year.
grammar: 세금 (segeum) = tax; 세금을 내다 = to pay tax; 매년 = every year.

english: The property tax bill came this month.
grammar: 재산세 (jaesanse) = property tax.

english: Income tax is more than I thought.
grammar: 소득세 (sodeukse) = income tax; -보다 = than.

english: I'm getting ready for year-end tax settlement.
grammar: 연말정산 (yeonmaljeongsan) = Korea's year-end tax adjustment.

english: I got a small tax refund.
grammar: 환급받다 (hwangeupbatda) = to receive a refund.

english: Tax is deducted from my salary.
grammar: 빠지다 → 빠져요 (ppajyeoyo) = to be taken out/deducted; 에서 = from.

english: I filed my taxes within the deadline.
grammar: 기한 (gihan) = deadline; 안에 = within; 신고 = a filing/report.

english: VAT is 10 percent.
grammar: 부가세 (bugase) = VAT; 십 퍼센트 (sip peosenteu) = ten percent (Sino).

english: Because of taxes, take-home pay shrinks.
grammar: 줄다 → 줄어요 (jureoyo) = to decrease; 실수령액 = take-home amount.

english: Tax calculations are so complicated.
grammar: 복잡하다 → 복잡해요 = to be complicated/complex.

english: I keep a household ledger every day.
grammar: 가계부 (gagyebu) = household account book; 가계부를 쓰다 = to keep it.

english: I tallied up this month's spending.
grammar: 지출 (jichul) = spending/expenses; 정리하다 = to organize/tally.

english: My spending is more than my income.
grammar: 수입 (suip) = income; -보다 더 = more than: 수입보다 더 많아요.

english: Living costs are high.
grammar: 생활비 (saenghwalbi) = living expenses; (돈이) 들다 = to cost.

english: I made a budget for this month.
grammar: 예산 (yesan) = budget; 예산을 짜다 → 짰어요 = to draw one up.

english: I mustn't go over budget.
grammar: -(으)면 안 돼요 = must not: 넘으면 안 돼요 (neomeumyeon an dwaeyo).

english: I need to cut down on eating out.
grammar: 줄이다 → 줄여야 해요 (juryeoya haeyo) = have to reduce; 외식비 = dining-out cost.

english: I even save on coffee.
grammar: 아끼다 → 아껴요 (akkyeoyo) = to save/spare, be frugal.

english: I often regret impulse buys.
grammar: 충동구매 (chungdong-gumae) = impulse purchase; 후회하다 = to regret.

english: I try to buy only what I need.
grammar: -(으)려고 해요 = intend to: 사려고 해요 (saryeogo haeyo) = plan to buy.

english: I give my kid an allowance every week.
grammar: 용돈 (yongdon) = pocket money/allowance; 매주 = every week.

english: The kids' education costs are really high.
grammar: 교육비 (gyoyukbi) = education costs; 들다 = to cost.

english: I paid the utility bills on time.
grammar: 공과금 (gonggwageum) = utility bills; 제때 = on time.

english: The electricity bill is higher than last month.
grammar: 요금 (yogeum) = a charge/fee (utilities, transport).

english: I saved a lot of money this month.
grammar: 아끼다 → 아꼈어요 (akkyeosseoyo) = saved, was frugal.

english: I want to manage money well.
grammar: 관리 (gwalli) = management; 돈 관리 = managing one's money.

english: My husband and I keep the ledger together.
grammar: -(이)랑 = with: 남편이랑 (nampyeon-irang) = with my husband.

english: Saving has become a habit now.
grammar: 절약 (jeollyak) = thrift/saving; -이 되다 → 됐어요 = became.

target: 제 목표는 빚을 다 갚는 거예요.
english: My goal is to pay off all my debt.
grammar: -는 거예요 = is (to do): 갚는 거예요 (gapneun geoyeyo) = is to pay off.

english: I'm very interested in personal finance.
grammar: 재테크 (jaeteukeu) = money management/investing to grow wealth.

english: These days I'm investing in stocks.
grammar: 투자하다 (tujahada) = to invest; 주식 = stocks/shares.

english: I invest a little at a time in small amounts.
grammar: 소액 (soaek) = a small sum; -으로 = with/in.

english: I'm happy my stocks went up a bit.
grammar: 오르다 → 올라서 (ollaseo) = because it rose (first-person 기뻐요).

english: I signed up for a fund too.
grammar: 가입하다 (gaipada) = to join/sign up; 펀드 = investment fund.

english: Investing always carries risk.
grammar: 위험 (wiheom) = risk/danger; 위험이 있다 = to carry risk.

english: I don't make reckless investments.
grammar: 무리한 (murihan) = excessive/overreaching (before a noun).

english: I'm preparing for retirement from now.
grammar: 노후 (nohu) = one's later years; 노후 준비 = retirement planning.

english: I pay into a pension every month.
grammar: 연금 (yeongeum) = pension; 넣다 = to put in.

english: I've gotten interested in real estate too.
grammar: 부동산 (budongsan) = real estate/property; 생기다 → 생겼어요 = came about.

english: Housing prices have risen a lot lately.
grammar: 집값 (jipgap) = house price; 오르다 → 올랐어요 = rose.

english: I started studying personal finance.
I got advice from an expert.
grammar: 전문가 (jeonmunga) = expert/specialist.

english: I want to spend money wisely.
grammar: 현명하게 (hyeonmyeonghage) = wisely; -게 makes an adverb.

english: I want to slowly become well-off.
grammar: 부자 (buja) = a rich person; -이/가 되다 = to become.

english: The exchange rate rose, so travel feels pricey.
grammar: 환율 (hwannyul) = exchange rate; 부담되다 → 부담돼요 = feels like a burden.

english: I exchanged money at the airport.
grammar: 환전하다 → 환전했어요 (hwanjeonhaesseoyo) = exchanged currency.

english: I carry only a little cash around.
grammar: 가지고 다니다 (gajigo danida) = to carry around with oneself.

english: These days I pay almost everything by mobile.
grammar: 거의 (geoui) = almost; 모바일로 = by mobile.

english: I lost my wallet, so I remade my card.
grammar: 잃어버리다 → 잃어버려서 (ireobeoryeoseo) = lost it, and so...

english: The bank app is really convenient.
grammar: 편하다 → 편해요 = to be convenient/comfortable.

english: I've come to enjoy saving.
grammar: 재미가 생기다 (jaemiga saenggida) = to come to enjoy something.

english: I spend money according to a plan.
grammar: 계획적으로 (gyehoekjeogeuro) = in a planned way, methodically.

english: I prepare retirement funds in advance.
grammar: 자금 (jageum) = funds/capital; 노후 자금 = retirement funds.

english: Health matters more than money.
grammar: -보다 더 = more than: 돈보다 (donboda) = more than money.
